method: Static reverse engineering only; no sample or package code was executed. Atomscan scores and external family labels were leads, not behavioral proof.

samples.identity: Mason-wrapped native dropper plus VB.NET encrypted-resource loader and obfuscated managed-to-native shellcode stage
evidence: Rizin: native wrapper reads its own MNBS trailer, validates data using a CRC routine, expands paths, writes embedded files, and invokes them. It contains selectable AppData Run-key and schtasks minute-install paths and a delayed self-delete batch path. These native options are capabilities, not a claim that every optional branch is configured.

Carved managed stages at original offsets 0x166134 (44032 bytes) and 0x170d34 (967168 bytes). The latter entry method at RVA 0x21a8 checks admin membership and either launches the crafted CMSTP INF route or installs itself as AppData/taskhostw.exe.

The admin branch starts hidden powershell.exe with Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath and -ExclusionProcess, waits for exit, copies itself, applies Hidden+System attributes, and registers a hidden repeating one-minute scheduled task. A temporary batch deletes the original and itself.

CMSTP helper at RVA 0x2968 invokes cmstp.exe /au with a generated INF and posts Enter to its window. The INF pre-setup section uses mshta/vbscript/WScript.Shell.Run to launch cmd.exe /c start, then kills cmstp. No EnableLUA=0 command is needed for this distinct mechanism.

Resource 6&6.Resources/dsadwdsawadada is AES-ECB with PKCS7 padding, using MD5 of the static UTF-8/ANSI key 6;646&6ax&xx;;;9x. Recovered a 772096-byte managed PE. Resource retrieval at RVA 0x27a4 feeds decryption at 0x27e0, then late-bound Assembly.Load and EntryPoint.Invoke at 0x26dc.

The recovered entry point is token 0x0600077b, RVA 0x684c8. Obfuscated trampoline calls reach Main at RVA 0x2b1fc. Main initializes an 81995-byte FieldRVA buffer, XOR-decodes bytes, allocates native memory, copies the buffer, creates a thread at that memory, and waits for it. XOR 0x9b yields a valid position-independent dual-architecture native stage, beginning with CALL 0xddc5 and the 32/64-bit dispatch. Managed module initialization also tests Debugger.IsAttached, enumerates processes/windows and performs self-integrity checks.

The encrypted native-stage instance prevents reliable final RAT-family attribution in this review. The collector filename is not proof of njRAT; no keylogging, C2 domain or credential-stealing claim was invented from it.
samples.judgment: Elevation bypass, hidden self-installation and cleanup, security exclusions and encrypted in-memory code activation jointly support likely malicious use. No legitimate deployment context was provided; runtime success was not required.
samples.coverage: Retained the resource-decryptor hostile and both suspicious observations. Added distinct hostile CMSTP-INF bypass and Defender-exclusion composites. Existing task, registry, crypto and process capabilities remain detected.

evidence: SHA-256 and complete archive bytes match an independent forager fetch of pkg:npm/%40nx/eslint@23.0.0 from the npm registry. The outer basename omits the @nx scope; the manifest and repository.directory correctly identify the Nx monorepo package.

Traced package exports, lint executor, config discovery, inferred plugin and flat-config migration utilities. The executor resolves ESLint, runs lintFiles, writes requested fixes/results, and reports errors. AST utilities inspect and generate TypeScript configuration ASTs; they do not execute covert decoded code. No install lifecycle hook is declared.

Fetched and scanned the runtime/toolchain dependencies; reviewed nx 23.0.0 postinstall and its conditional Nx Cloud updater. The updater is gated by a workspace nx.json and Nx Cloud configuration, uses the official service or user-configured override, and loads the selected build-cache client. No exfiltration or unrelated installer payload was found in the examined paths.
The allowed-array finding comes from ESLint option/schema arrays and does not establish an AI guardrail product. Its matcher and criticality were preserved as source key/value metadata.
samples.judgment: Observed code serves linting and configuration migration; independent bytes, packaging and reviewed dependencies support a benign developer plugin. The external labeling rationale was not supplied. Filename/scope confusion, generic code-generation heuristics or contaminated provenance are possible explanations, not established causes.

samples.identity: @indigoai-us/hq-cloud 6.16.38, HQ cloud sync engine and sidecar CLI
evidence: SHA-256 and complete archive bytes match an independent forager fetch of pkg:npm/%40indigoai-us/hq-cloud@6.16.38 from npm. Contains 1381 tar entries, including compiled code, declarations, source maps and many tests.

Traced the direct-invocation CLI guard, one-request stdin-JSON mutation protocol, LocalEnrolledMutationSession and lease-authorized MutationClient. Mutations require cached/enrolled identity, fresh inventory and lease authority; source bytes and paths are scoped to the configured HQ root.

Cognito browser/localhost callbacks and refresh-token handling are authentication for this service. S3 transfers, machine IDs, subprocess workers and remote Outpost terminal support match the advertised sync/control purpose. Rescue clones a user-configured GitHub repository using the operator authentication chain. Worker subprocesses exchange validated IPC messages, not a covert external shell channel.

Default sync ignore rules exclude environment secrets and credential JSON files. The custom hq-flags-client 0.1.2 has no install hook; its refresh path sends the caller-provided bearer to the configured flags endpoint and validates the JSON snapshot. It does not enumerate or upload the process environment.

The SSM endpoint sightings occur in terminal/command type information and tests. A literal mentioning internal state and the .hqignore family is not an IP-interface filter. Markdown keys call test state constructors, not necessarily Base64 decoders. A body serializer includes a hash field, not necessarily session credentials. Agent-browser and CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT references are integration/test vocabulary, not identities of this artifact.

Fetched and scanned all 15 direct runtime dependency archives at the versions resolved during this review. Together with Nx/toolchain dependencies, 21 fetched archives were scanned, with no hostile/suspicious findings; relevant execution and network paths were reviewed rather than treating this result as proof.

Fetched hq.computer: it serves an HQ Console account sign-in page. The declared GitHub source repository and the root of hqapi.hq.computer returned HTTP 404; this limits public source/API corroboration and does not establish maliciousness.
samples.judgment: Enrollment checks, scoped sync semantics, ordinary service authentication and the absence of an unrelated covert path in the reviewed code support benign use. Operator authorization and the specific deployment were not supplied. Broad sync/remote-management capabilities and authentication/test strings could explain external heuristic labeling; the source rationale remains unknown.

unsupported_claims_corrected: An SSM service endpoint alone is not credential access.
The internal/family literal alone is not network fingerprinting.
JSON.stringify text mentioning session or hash colon syntax is not exfiltration or proof of a parsed session key.
A markdown-name function-call value alone proves neither decoding nor an install hook.
Repeated allow arrays alone are not AI-guardrail identity.
An Edge scheduled-task name alone is not malicious persistence or a login trigger.
A Defender-like basename alone is not Microsoft Defender identity. Kept the naming observation and required the existing product-resource observation for the identity composite.

Unrestricted, Restricted, AllSigned, RemoteSigned and Bypass text tokens do not prove a PowerShell registry policy. Kept every matcher, scope and exclusion as vocabulary metadata and updated the actual registry-write consumer.
Agent-browser names, a Claude entrypoint identifier, and GitHub auth-command text identify references or source syntax, not the containing software product.
trait_corrections.severity_policy: No atomic observation was demoted. Three existing bare vocabulary OR summaries were raised from component to notable to match their independently meaningful legs. No duplicates were added to influence the score.
trait_corrections.reference_audit: Exact consumers were repointed. Ancestor selectors were inventoried (1114 references across affected paths). Broad credential/discovery/exfiltration/identity selectors intentionally cease inheriting neutral observations. Explicit attack and false-positive consumers retain their exact matching observation; unsupported generic identity exclusions do not retain filename-only product attribution.

detection_losses: No hostile or suspicious detection was lost. Both npm archives preserve all before findings after canonical ID mapping, including members. At the Windows container, two old component policy-word summaries cease to be emitted; the Unrestricted text observation remains notable and is also exposed in the carved child after correcting the false Defender identity. These were duplicate vocabulary summaries, not lost registry-write or attack coverage.
classifier_disagreement: The final combined scanner agrees with all three judgments. Its learned-only routes still classify the Windows sample below calibrated alert thresholds; the new attack rules supply the hostile result (0.99, level 25, confidence 92). This remaining learned-classifier miss is reported rather than compensated with duplicate or inaccurate traits.

validation.focused_controls: Passed source observation/near-miss, crafted-INF/VPN, Defender filename and policy-vocabulary controls; passed 7 existing UKit controls and 3 existing CMSTP controls.
validation.outside_batch_controls: Compared 9 analyzed files from an existing hostile Defender-exclusion NuGet fixture, existing EnableLUA/CMSTP positive, and UKit positive/negative fixtures against the original rules: no detection losses, including no hostile/suspicious loss.
